messages:
jinwoo: FYI: Canary perf regression after autotuner tweak — 95p latency up ~18% on chat-prod-sim. Attaching quick profiler summary I grabbed from the canary node.

jinwoo: profiler summary (top lines):
```
GPU: A100-80GB
continuous_batcher: avg_batch_size=1.6, median_seq=48, p95_seq=120
kernel_launch_overhead_ms: small_block=1.8, wide_block=0.6
kernel_exec_ms_per_token: small_block=0.6, wide_block=1.2 (but drops to 0.5 with KV reuse)
observed_95_latency_ms: before=120, after=142
```

eva: Oof. Is this the change that bumped small-block preference? @matt

matt: Yep — autotuner commit 2026-03-15 adjusted the memory footprint penalty. That shifted cost scores toward small_block for a bunch of seqlen/batch combos.

tim: What are the trace distributions (batch size / seq len) that actually hit the canary workload?

jinwoo: Continuous batcher traces: many single-turn requests, long tail of short messages. avg batch_size 1.6, median seq_len 48. With small batches + short seqs, launch overhead becomes the dominant cost.

sara: Kernel selector rules dump I pulled from canary: 
```
# simplified selector rules
- if seq_len <= 64 and est_mem < 10GB -> prefer small_block_kernel
- elif batch_size >= 8 -> prefer wide_block_kernel
- else -> use autotuner score
```

eva: So the tuner is favoring small_block because of memory and throughput estimates, but it doesn't account for per-launch overhead which kills short-batch latency. The old wide_block choice had higher exec_time but fewer launches.

matt: Correct — current cost function is basically: score = throughput_est - mem_penalty. It ignores launch_ms * expected_calls. We never calibrated calls_per_token for continuous batching patterns.

tim: Options here: add launch_cost to the autotuner score; introduce a "sticky kernel" routing for continuous batcher (keep using the same kernel for repeated shapes); or increase the batching window to raise avg batch size (latency tradeoff).

jinwoo: Also note KV-cache behavior: for chat workloads we often reuse KV cache, which makes wide_block exec_time shrink (favors wide kernels). Small_block path doesn't benefit as much from KV-optimized GEMMs. So exec_time_est needs a cached_kv factor.

sara: Proposal: extend autotuner model: 
```
cost = launch_ms * est_calls_per_req + exec_ms_per_token * est_tokens + mem_penalty - kv_reuse_gain
```
where exec_ms_per_token and launch_ms should be per-kernel, per-arch measurements.

matt: I'll prototype adding launch_ms into the tuner. Need microbench numbers for all kernels across archs and seq ranges. @ops-bot can we schedule the microbench suite on canary/A100s?

ops-bot: Scheduled job: kernel_microbench/arch-A100/shortseq started at 1805554600. Results will be posted in this thread when done.

tim: Quick heuristic we can ship faster: if avg_batch_size < 2 and median_seq < 64 and (launch_ms / exec_ms) > 1.5 -> prefer wide_block. Cheap to implement and likely to remove most regressions.

eva: :thumbsup: Also add a canary regression alert that fires when an autotuner policy change coincides with >10% increase in 95p latency for chat-sim. We should block policy rollouts automatically until we validate microbench numbers.

jinwoo: Action items: matt -> autotuner metric change (launch_ms + kv factor), tim -> batcher heuristics & sticky kernel routing, sara -> collect KV reuse profiles and annotate exec_ms. I'll file issues and follow up.

deploy-bot: Created issue #987: "autotune: include kernel launch cost and KV reuse in cost model" (assigned: matt/tim/sara).

matt: Starting a local branch with launch cost integration, will push a PR and attach perf numbers.

jinwoo: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow after the microbench runs.
